The HAB/Freiburg scholarly diary introduction explicitly equates 23 October with 2 November and identifies Torstensson against Leopold Wilhelm and Piccolomini’s imperial-Saxon army. Identity review (attacker; original CDB90 name SW ARMY): The HAB/Freiburg introduction identifies the Swedish field command at the second Breitenfeld battle. Identity review (defender; original CDB90 name IMP ARMY): The scholarly introduction explicitly identifies the imperial-Saxon command under Leopold Wilhelm and Piccolomini. This is the aggregate IMP ARMY record, not separately quantified coalition members. Historical published participant Q12548 is replaced by this event-local aggregate; its exact original item and P710 statement citations are preserved here as provenance. It is not an additional separately scaled component.

Q1059732.note: Reviewed CDB90 match 100, pinned revision e0b35ec4d798cec3bb4e6970c0f6bb7aa69e2f4c. CDB90 (CAA Database of Battles, Version 1990), tidy data maintained by Jeffrey B. Arnold. Original US Army Concepts Analysis Agency data; revised data licensed ODC-BY. Original force designations and strength interpretations are retained with each quantity. Each side is one aggregate force, including any coalition; its total is not allocated among members. Personnel casualties are not deaths. Source estimates and adjudged error margins are not statistical confidence intervals. Equipment and tactical movements are not established by this dataset. Match review: Approve the exact whole battle after restoring its 15–16 October 1793 extent. The Hauts-de-France Inventaire record explicitly gives both days, and the Ministry of Culture identifies Jourdan opposite Clerfayt’s Austrian army. CDB90 represents the French Army of the North and the Austrian force at this engagement as two aggregate armies (44000/23000 initial personnel), not the whole First Coalition or all forces besieging Maubeuge. The institutional records establish the event, dates and opposed commands; they do not independently certify the tabulated counts or the 4500/3000 casualty estimates. No siege-garrison count is added. Identity review (attacker; original CDB90 name FRENCH ARMY OF THE NORTH): Original CDB90 FRENCH ARMY OF THE NORTH, localized and bounded to Wattignies. Ministry of Culture evidence identifies Jourdan, with Carnot and Duquesnoy; no separate commander or garrison strength is created. Identity review (defender; original CDB90 name AUSTRIAN ARMY): Original AUSTRIAN ARMY, bounded to the engagement. The Ministry of Culture identifies the opposing command under Clerfayt; this label does not incorporate the entire coalition or add the separate Maubeuge siege force.

Q2888281.note: Reviewed CDB90 match 160, pinned revision e0b35ec4d798cec3bb4e6970c0f6bb7aa69e2f4c. CDB90 (CAA Database of Battles, Version 1990), tidy data maintained by Jeffrey B. Arnold. Original US Army Concepts Analysis Agency data; revised data licensed ODC-BY. Original force designations and strength interpretations are retained with each quantity. Each side is one aggregate force, including any coalition; its total is not allocated among members. Personnel casualties are not deaths. Source estimates and adjudged error margins are not statistical confidence intervals. Equipment and tactical movements are not established by this dataset. Match review: Approve the whole 17–18 April 1847 battle after restoring the opening day. The Library of Congress catalogues the contemporary McClellan/Turnbull map explicitly for both days; U.S. Army CMH identifies Scott against Santa Anna’s entrenched army (about 12000), while AMEDD dates the victory to 18 April. CDB90 initial estimates remain 8500 U.S./12000 Mexican personnel. Its 431/4000 casualty figures are not deaths. CMH instead reports 64 U.S. killed+353 wounded and about 1000–1200 Mexican casualties separately from about 3000 prisoners; these differently tabulated estimates are disclosed, not substituted, summed into deaths, or assumed exactly equal to CDB90. Both source strength rows have no reinforcements. Identity review (attacker; original CDB90 name US ARMY): CMH identifies Scott’s U.S. army advancing through Cerro Gordo. The CDB90 quantity is the initial battle force, not all U.S. troops in Mexico. Historical published participant Q30 is replaced by this event-local aggregate; its exact original item and P710 statement citations are preserved here as provenance. It is not an additional separately scaled component. Identity review (defender; original CDB90 name MEX ARMY): CMH identifies Santa Anna’s entrenched army at this pass, estimated there at about 12000. This is an event-local force, not the country’s entire armed forces.
